failureMessage: the update lands a seeded pack on every member but skips the home, so a newly seeded pack reaches the whole fleet except this repo, invisibly

requireIndexCoverage.what: the "{pack}" pack flags seededByDefault in its manifest but is not declared here
requireIndexCoverage.fix: add "{pack}" to the "packs" array — the update skips the home, so this repo's declaration is hand-maintained; a deliberate opt-out is an acceptance with a reason instead

failureMessage: a legacy tolerance nobody is scheduled to remove is a permanent feature wearing a temporary name, and its holders are never told to move off it

matchLines.what: {match} declares a legacy tolerance with no scheduled removal above it
matchLines.fix: put `// @legacy-tolerance advisory:<rule-id|none> retire:#<issue>` directly above it: the rule that tells a holder to migrate, and the issue whose merge deletes this code

matchLines.what: {match} is not a readable tolerance annotation
matchLines.fix: write it as `// @legacy-tolerance advisory:<rule-id|none> retire:#<issue>` with nothing after — a grep for this token is the register, and an unparseable form is not in it

failureMessage: a pack's RULES.md is written several times a day, and a whole-file re-apply onto a moved main deletes lessons with nothing going red

forbidRemovedLinesMatching.fix: re-apply your edit onto the fetched file as an insertion, and say in the PR when a rule is deliberately retired

failureMessage: the clones here are shallow, so git pull finds no common ancestor, and nothing of value is ever on this repo's local main

guardToolCalls.what: a git pull
guardToolCalls.fix: git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main

failureMessage: there is no gh CLI here, and every repo-scoped api.github.com call 403s ("GitHub access is not enabled for this session"), so a shell poll reports "still running" until it times out

guardToolCalls.what: a GitHub read through the shell: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: read the head sha's check runs with the GitHub MCP tools (pull_request_read get_check_runs, get_check_run)

guardToolCalls.what: a Monitor polling GitHub through the shell: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: read the head sha's check runs with the GitHub MCP tools on a rolling backoff; a shell poll here never sees the run finish

failureMessage: a padded sleep waits on nothing nameable; a guard that would not stand as the whole test is sleeping and calling it polling
fix: name the condition awaited — a run's status, a file's arrival, a deadline — and wait on that

guardToolCalls.what: a bare "{match}"
a counted loop with nothing but a sleep in its body: "{match}"

failureMessage: a bash glob without globstar runs green over a subset — packs/*/test/*.test.mjs reaches 125 of 314 files and says nothing; node --test <dir> at least fails outright with Cannot find module

guardToolCalls.what: the suite run through a glob: "{match}"
node --test with no files named

failureMessage: git commit -a stages every modified file, and a later branch -D discards the in-progress edits it swept up

guardToolCalls.what: a commit with -a
guardToolCalls.fix: stage the files this commit is about by name; isolate pending edits first

failureMessage: a hook is a guest in the harness: the runner alone exits or writes, and a judge that does prints an error on every call
fix: return the verdict — { block, reason } or { context } — and let hook-runner.mjs write it

matchLines.what: a judge touching the process itself: {match}

failureMessage: a migration's plan, status and remaining work live in its tracking issue, never a MIGRATION.md beside the design

forbidTrackedPathsMatching.fix: move what is still live into the tracking issue (writing-migration-plans) and delete the file

failureMessage: the executor reads only this repository: its sessions carry no member's scope and its probes fetch anonymously, so this verification can never pass

guardToolCalls.what: a verification line reading another repository: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: reproduce the premise on an object this repo owns, or file the verification on that repo

guardToolCalls.what: a probe fetching the GitHub API: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: probe a public raw or Pages URL instead, or make it a Verify: line about this repository

failureMessage: add_repo attaches nothing the git proxy does not already serve for a public repository

guardToolCalls.what: an add_repo for "{field}"
guardToolCalls.fix: for a public repository's files, git clone --depth 1 (about two seconds); add_repo only for a private one, or for its issues and pull requests

failureMessage: an image rendered from a scratch harness reads as the product unless its caption says otherwise

guardToolCalls.what: a screenshot from the scratchpad sent without saying it came from a scratch harness
guardToolCalls.fix: say in the caption that it is rendered from a scratch test harness, not just what the widget shows

failureMessage: MEMBER covers any org member and COLLABORATOR includes read-only ones, both broader than push access

matchLines.fix: read the collaborators permission endpoint (GET /repos/../collaborators/../permission) for the actor instead

failureMessage: fielded workers are stale callers of an instantly-current flow module, so a removed export wedges every member on its next run

forbidRemovedLinesMatching.what: removes an export from a fielded flow module: {match}
forbidRemovedLinesMatching.fix: empty the export instead, and say at its definition why it stays

failureMessage: a year's last digit wraps to 0 in 2030, so an identifier anchored on it collides four years out

matchLines.what: anchors a year on its last digit: {match}
matchLines.fix: subtract an epoch (year - 2020) so the encoding survives the decade boundary

failureMessage: git checkout -- restores from the index, destroying uncommitted work as thoroughly as the mutation it undoes

guardToolCalls.what: a working-tree restore: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: commit or stage the real edit first, and only mutate a file whose current state you are ready to throw away

failureMessage: a JSON round trip rewrites indent, key order and escapes while nothing fails and tests stay green

guardToolCalls.what: a settings file rewritten by re-serialising it: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: patch the file as anchored text instead

failureMessage: an initiative's DESIGN.md reads as a description of how the system works; without a status on its first screen a reader takes an unbuilt proposal for the current state

checkEachFile.what: carries no status banner in its first seven lines
checkEachFile.fix: open it with `> **Status: not implemented.** …` or `> **Status: in flight.** …`; a built system's design doc has no third status — delete it whole instead

failureMessage: a loop body of `:` yields nothing, so the shell spins at full tilt and the session answers nobody until a person interrupts it

guardToolCalls.what: a loop that spins without waiting: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: sleep inside the loop body and bound the wait — or drop the loop: a background task's completion arrives as a notification

failureMessage: the canon home carries no .claudinite/shared/ at all, so a module invoked through that path is Cannot find module and the sweep the session believed it ran never ran

guardToolCalls.what: an engine module run through the mount: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: drop the prefix and run it from the repo root (node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs); a member's checkout cloned into this session keeps the mount path, and needs the cd that says so

failureMessage: the pre-edit skill guard reads Edit, Write and NotebookEdit only, so a shell write carries its skill requirement to Stop, after the work the skill was there to shape

guardToolCalls.what: a skill-scoped file written through the shell: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: write it with Write, or Edit it after a read — those are the calls the guard sees

failureMessage: a check inside its two-week since grace reports ADVISORY, so a BLOCKING-only filter reads your own new check as silent and the violations it found as none

guardToolCalls.what: a sweep read through a BLOCKING-only filter: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: read the whole output — the advisory lines carry every check still inside its since grace, your own new one among them

failureMessage: a worktree-isolated agent's shell guard refuses a command over the word git, so a branch carrying it in its own name cannot be created there under any spelling

guardToolCalls.what: a worktree-isolated dispatch mandating a branch named over git: "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: name the branch without the word git (perf/fixtures, not perf/git-fixtures) — the child cannot rename it afterwards either

failureMessage: the newest .jsonl under ~/.claude/projects is always the transcript of the session running the scan, so the script reads its own run rather than the one asked about

guardToolCalls.what: a {tool} locating a session transcript by newest mtime
guardToolCalls.fix: resolve <sessionId>.jsonl with findTranscript from packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs; a transcript never leaves its container, so a script for another session takes that session's id as an argument

failureMessage: a canon path in a migration record fails open — an unreadable probe reads as "not capable", a missing template is skipped — so a move leaves the record silently inert

checkSetValues.what: the record names {value}, which is not a path in this tree
checkSetValues.fix: repoint it at the file's current path; where the target is gone for good, delete the probe or materialization naming it rather than leave one that can never fire

failureMessage: the owner writes with hyphens; a long dash is a model's habit, and a JSON round trip turns the ones already there into escapes nobody meant to write

forbidAddedLinesMatching.fix: use a hyphen, a comma or a full stop; a line the change merely moved keeps its text, so re-add it as it was

failureMessage: git's auto-gc detaches and keeps writing under .git after the command returns, so the fixture's removal races it: the suite passes locally and CI fails with ENOTEMPTY

checkEachFile.what: builds a throwaway git repo with a spawn of its own, so git's housekeeping outlives the command that started it
checkEachFile.fix: call the shared runner - `import { git } from '<relative>/engine-tests/helpers.mjs'`, then `git(root, 'init', '-q')` - or spawn with its GIT_CONFIG env, which holds gc.autoDetach and maintenance.auto off

failureMessage: reference-integrity is work-scoped and sees only a path the same branch deletes, so a citation an earlier move stranded sends every later session into nothing

checkSetValues.what: the prose cites {value}, which is not a path in this tree
checkSetValues.fix: repoint it at the file's current path, or drop the citation where the sentence reads without one

failureMessage: a pipe write is asynchronous and process.exit() drops what is still queued, so a caller capturing the output reads a truncated answer under a clean status

forbidAddedLinesMatching.what: "{match}" prints and then exits hard on one line
forbidAddedLinesMatching.fix: set process.exitCode and let the process end, adding a `return` where the exit was also ending the flow - or exit from the write's own callback, as hook-runner.mjs does

failureMessage: a pickaxe or --reverse walk answers with the earliest commit the CHECKOUT reaches, so on a shallow clone it hands back the clone's own horizon as the repository's history

matchLines.what: asks history for its earliest hit: {match}
matchLines.fix: probe `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` and say so rather than answering from the horizon, or `git fetch --unshallow` first; a walk bounded by a `<ref>..<ref>` range is out of scope

failureMessage: renderRunCost prints only the words RUN_PHASES names, so a phase timed under any other word is measured and then dropped, and the fold never sees what it cost

whenSetEmpty.what: nothing under packs/claudinite-tasks/src/ opens a run phase under a literal word
whenSetEmpty.fix: the timer's call shape moved, so repoint "phasesTimed" at how a phase is opened now, or retire this check if no run times itself any more

whenSetEmpty.what: RUN_PHASES names no phase word, so every timed phase would read as one this vocabulary does not have
whenSetEmpty.fix: the declaration's shape moved, so repoint "phasesNamed" at where the per-workflow phase lists are spelled now

checkSetPairs.what: the run times a phase under '{value}', which RUN_PHASES does not name
checkSetPairs.fix: add '{value}' to that workflow's list in RUN_PHASES, in the order the run executes it, or time the phase under a word the vocabulary already carries

failureMessage: a generated file's banner is read by everyone and heeded by nobody: it repeats what the file's name or its directory already says, and every reader pays the line
fix: delete the banner where the generator writes it, not in the file it wrote
